previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for confusion and a fall, with worsening back pain. He has a history of hepatitis C cirrhosis, recurrent hepatic encephalopathy, and prior vertebral osteomyelitis. Evaluation revealed hepatic encephalopathy likely triggered by pain and stress, with no evidence of acute infection. MRI showed new acute compression fractures at T9, T11, and L1, but no active osteomyelitis. A possible aortic valve vegetation seen on TTE was ruled out by TEE. He was treated with continued lactulose and rifaximin for encephalopathy, optimized diuretic therapy, and initiated on high-dose vitamin D and testosterone replacement for osteoporosis. A TLSO brace was fitted for spinal support. His mental status and pain improved, and he was discharged to extended care with follow-up plans.

For the past month, he has found himself gasping for breath 
after walking even one or two blocks, after which he feels very 
lightheaded, sometimes necessitating him to sit down or hold on 
to a wall to prevent himself from falling.  He has had 5 or so 
of these presyncope episodes in the past year.  Two days prior 
to presentation, an episode of similar presyncope occurred, but 
he was not able to catch himself, and he fainted and fell to the 
floor.  Bystanders told him he was out for only a few seconds.  
There was no associated shaking or incontinence.  He felt no 
irregular heart beats.  He got up and rested and his symptoms 
resolved.  
Patient also notes lower extremity weakness and dull aching, 
mostly in his quads, worse with increased exertion.  He rarely 
feels symptoms in his gluts or calves.  At times, he has had 
trouble getting up from chairs.  This problem has been 
extensively worked up by his hepatologist, Dr. ___.  MRI was 
done recently at the beginning of ___ that showed no 
evidence of cord impingement.  TSH and CPK were also within 
normal limits.  
Patient denies any chest pain with exertion. He also denies 
numbness, tingling, headache, dysarthria during any of these 
episodes. 
Patient waited 3 days before presenting to the hospital because 
he knew his symptoms would not recur if he rested in bed.

morning, so does not feel any shortness of breath,

Brief Hospital Course:
Primary Reason for Admission:  
___ with ESLD presents with 2 months of worsening dyspnea on 
exertion, several episodes of presyncope and one episode of 
syncope, as well as progressively worsening ___ weakness.

Active Diagnoses:
# Syncope/Presyncope. Initial ddx for syncope included pulmonary 
hypertension/portopulmonary hypertension (which he is at risk 
for given ESLD), CAD (given patient's new Twave inversions, and 
exertional-related symptoms), or general deconditioning.  
Patient was already ruled out for PE in ED and cardiac enzymes 
are negative x2 with no symptoms of angina to suggest ACS.  TTE 
on day of admission showed TR gradient of 60mmHg, up from 30mmHg 
in ___, consistent with pulmonary hypertension.  This also 
explains patient's progressive dyspnea on exertion.  RHC 
___ showed severe pulm htn, mPAP 45mmHg with 10mmHg 
increase in mPAP when sitting up.  mPAP dropped with O2, but was 
unresponsive to NO.  PFTs showed normal lung volumes and 
slightly reduced (but not dramatically reduced) DLCO.  
Continuous O2 monitoring at night showed hat patient's O2 sat 
dips down to low ___, sometimes high ___, while sleeping.  
Pulmonology team recommended starting Sildinofil, home oxygen, 
and getting an outpatient sleep study.  ___ and RF to rule out 
other causes of pulmonary hypertension were negative.  Patient 
was also diuresed to improve cardiac status.  He was started on 
home oxygen at night and was prescribed Sildenafil, but was 
awaiting insurance approval at the time of discharge.

Chronic diagnoses:
# ___ weakness. No obvious neurological deficits on exam and 
patient denies sensory loss or incotinence.  Patient received an 
MRI two weeks ago that was negative for cord 
compression/impingement.  Patient states this is a chronic issue 
for him, however, it has worsened over the past few months.  Ddx 
includes cord compression (ruled out by MRI earlier this month), 
claudication (unlikely given distribution of his ache in his 
quads), hypothyroidism (but nl TSH earlier this month), myopathy 
(normal CPK earlier this month), or general deconditioning.  No 
need to repeat MRI obtained earlier this month since patient 
does not have signs of cord compression.  Physical therapy saw 
patient in house and felt he was safe for ambulation.

# ESLD:  ESLD from ___ and on liver transplant list.  Sober for 
___ years.  Has hx of hepatic encephalopathy with sleep/wake 
inversion and prior episodes of SBP.  On admission, there was no 
need for paracentesis since no exam findings of ascites. He was 
continued on lactulose, rifaximin for hepatic encephalopathy, 
his diuretic regimen (plus additional diuresis on top of that), 
and nadolol.  

# Chronic pain:  Patient has chronic back pain from chornic 
compression fractures.  He was continued on his home morphine 
and dilaudid regimen.

# Osteoporosis:  Severe osteoporisis that began after his 
episode of osteomyelitis, leading to chronic compression 
fractures.  He was continued on home calcium and vitamin D.  

Transitional Issues:
Patient was encouraged to set up appointment for outpatient 
sleep study (for which his PCP has already referred him), as OSA 
may be a reversible cause of pulmonary hypertension. Per patient 
report he was in the process of scheduling this appointment. 

Sildenafil pprescription was provided for the patient, although 
his prio authorization had not yet come through at the time of 
discharge. Per pulmonary, it was ok to discharge off this 
medication, with oxygen.

Will follow-up with Dr. ___ in Pulmonary ___ and will 
continue to work to get insurance approval for Sildenafil.

New home oxygen therapy was arranged for the patient on 
discharge.
